met_analysis:
The Deep Depression over north coastal Odisha and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal moved west- northwestwards with a speed of 12 kmph during past 6 hours, and lay centred at 0830 hrs IST of today, the 28th July 2026, over north interior Odisha and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal, near latitude 21.9°N and longitude 86.8°E, about 10 km southeast of Baripada (Odisha), 40 km north-northwest of Balasore (Odisha), 80 km southwest of Midnapore (West Bengal), 120 km south-southeast of Jamshedpur (Jharkhand) and 140 km east-northeast of Keonjhargarh (Odisha).It is very likely to continue to move west-northwestwards across north Odisha, south Jharkhand and north Chhattisgarh during next 24 Hrs.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Anupgarh, Pilani, Hamirpur, Daltonganj, centre of Deep Depressionover north interior Odisha and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal, thence southeastwards towards Northeast Bay of Bengal.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northern parts of Central Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood now lies over southwest Uttar Pradesh at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over northwest Madhya Pradesh at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over northeast Assam and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
A Western Disturbance seen as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 32°N.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The trough from cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood to cyclonic circulation associated with Deep Depressionover north coastal Odisha and adjoining Gangetic West Bengal coasts across Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand at 3.1 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over east-central Arabian sea and adjoining Konkan coast at 5.8 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
